pairs.subject: federated-benchmark-sharing
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/collective/types.rs:77 The wire digest carries a contributor-chosen, high-cardinality rubric hash. provenance.rs:9-16 calls this hash a linkage key and refuses to publish it, yet it still crosses to the hub, where it is stored per contributor and backs the `?rubric=` membership filter. The hub ends up holding a correlation channel finer than anything it publishes.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/collective/types.rs:77 Everything else conforms: RunStat is aggregate-only, variance is None for a single-run bucket (merge.rs:221), the schema is additive with MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION, and dataset_version is consumed locally. The rubric fingerprint fails the 'could a reader correlate two digests' test.

crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:334 bucket_cost gives 2 significant figures and is applied in the digest (merge.rs:332). Latency percentiles ship at exact ms, though, and the leaderboard publishes one source's exact max p95 (types.rs:182). The merged avg_cost_usd is published at r6 rather than the 2-significant-figure schema resolution.
crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:323 Under-floor buckets are dropped, not flagged, and their count is returned for disclosure as buckets_withheld. low_confidence is a separate display floor.

crates/core/src/collective/vocab.rs:47 A 10-member closed list. The classifier is total, matches most-specific-first and falls back to `general`. A hub clamp exists, and tests assert membership for garbage input.

crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:364 The top source is winsorized to 0.8 only when a row has 2 or more sources, and the spread/CI use the same weights (merge.rs:400). max_source_share and the raw n_cases are disclosed.

crates/core/src/collective/vocab.rs:89 A schema-derived test forces every categorical wire field to name its clamp ('every field, every version'). The arithmetic gate itself is in the API and is judged there.
crates/core/src/collective/contribution.rs:72 ContributionRecord records what was already published, with the consent envelope and content hash, so a later push can be gated as unchanged.

pairs.registryProposal: aggregate-only-digests says identifying inputs are consumed locally and only consequences ship. A cross-contributor commensurability fact (do two sources share a rubric?) cannot be computed locally, so the technique should say how to ship such a field: e.g. derive it only from shared/public rubric definitions, never from instance-local ids, or bucket it into a small vocabulary.

pairs.subject: federated-benchmark-sharing
pairs.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/collective.rs:97 When a stored quality, pass_rate, cost or count is missing or mistyped, the Firestore decoder substitutes 0 instead of skipping the entry with a warning. A zero-case phantom still counts toward n_contributors in the merge. Meanwhile a missing string or timestamp makes list() abort through collect::<Result>, so one bad document takes down the whole leaderboard read for every reader.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/collective.rs:97 Consumption repairs the entry (the default substitution forbidden by nullable-never-zero) or fails hard (collective.rs:123). It never skips, warns and counts.
crates/store-firestore/src/contributions.rs:3 Firestore backs the contribution ledger, the record of what was already published. An unknown status is surfaced, not coerced (contributions.rs:55-60).
